title: Arm joint calibration
purpose: Match the supported arm's free-motion response to measured commands and joint feedback, then test on separate recordings.

execution.boundary: The guided section selects the installed executor and default parameter scope; reporting requirements are enforced by the report builder. Other sections describe the reusable procedure. Existing Python recipes own executable bounds, loss, optimizer and gates. This JSON does not install code, controllers or motion generators.

guided.default_scope_notice: Start with stiffness and damping for each declared joint group. Add armature, friction, effort or delay explicitly; insufficient evidence never silently removes a requested parameter.

setup_inputs.meaning: USD and dependencies, asset digest, joint names/limits, units, base mounting and supported Newton runtime.
Task goal and intended deployment interface; free-motion calibration alone does not prove task transfer.
Real signal to USD joint map, ordering, sign, units and zero offset, with operator/source confirmation.
Real and simulated modes, command semantics, update rate, interpolation/filtering, limits, gains, compensation, software versions and confirmation provenance.
Attached gripper/tool identity, state, mounting transform, mass/COM/inertia, held payload or explicit no-payload declaration. Unknown values remain unresolved.
Existing command and feedback logs, clock semantics, timestamps, units, independent trial IDs and train/held-out assignment. Absence leads to collection planning, not invented measurements.
Per-parameter bounds, initial values, ownership, units and source. No portable guess for physical friction/inertia or safe hardware settings.

Required before real collection: approved starting pose, clear workspace, velocity/acceleration/effort limits, stop procedure and responsible operator. Simulation screening is not safety certification.

parameter_families.evidence: Timestamped commands and q/dq with excitation across the intended speed/frequency range
parameter_families.caveat: Effective closed-loop response; individual physical constants may be confounded.

parameter_families.evidence: Acceleration-rich q/dq plus known controller/tool model
parameter_families.caveat: Requires independent sensitivity; do not assume all parameters are identifiable from one chirp.

parameter_families.evidence: Slow bidirectional motion and reversals; torque if available and calibrated
parameter_families.caveat: Controller compensation and payload can confound friction.

parameter_families.evidence: Actual dispatched commands, synchronized clocks and feedback
parameter_families.caveat: Missing clock facts cannot be repaired just by collecting more motion.
Never generate saturation-seeking hardware motions automatically.

collection.reuse_first: Inspect existing evidence and reuse sufficient train/held-out recordings.
collection.missing_evidence: Request supported collection experiments for the unresolved parameters, with exact joint commands, timing, expected signals and explicit deferred parameters.
families: independent held-out multisine or different sweep
collection.preview: Where a scene/preview adapter is available, replay the exact exported commands and record a labeled video. Otherwise report preview unavailable, not passed.
collection.safety: Collection is a proposal until the operator approves the robot-specific profile. This recipe is not a hardware authorization.

validation.procedure: Lock train/held-out split, bounds, objective and runtime before fitting. Use held-out trajectories only for validation; disclose any later model-selection use.
validation.report: Baseline and calibrated metric, per-episode regressions, stability, declared gates, parameter uncertainty, provenance and activation decision from the package writer.
validation.scope: Arm free motion only. Gripper attachment is context, not proof of gripping force. Real task transfer requires separate evidence.
